reading.title: Prefixes That Map Where and What
reading.purpose: Learn how the prefixes inter-, sub-, and non- give clear clues to word meanings.
paras: Long words look hard until you split them into parts. Three prefixes, inter-, sub-, and non-, act like road signs. They point straight to what a word means.

The prefix inter- means "between" or "among." An interstate road links states across a land. An international sports meet brings teams from two or more lands together. Where two roads cross each other, you find an intersection. In a radio interview, two people trade questions and answers.

The prefix sub- means "under" or "smaller part." A submarine is a ship built to move deep under water. In a book, a subheading sits under a main title to guide your eyes. If a grower splits one big field into small lots, they subdivide it.

The prefix non- just means "not." A nonfiction book shares real facts, not made-up tales. Silly talk with no real sense is nonsense. A nonstop flight goes from start to end without one break along the way.
When you spot inter-, sub-, or non- at the front of a word, you already have a strong clue.

choices: to travel deep beneath the surface of the ocean
to split a large part into smaller parts
to write a main title at the top of a book
to connect two roads that cross each other

qs.q: A reporter sits down with a firefighter to ask questions about fire safety. Which word from the reading names this meeting?
qs.why: Paragraph 2 explains that during an interview, questions and answers pass back and forth between two people.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Textbooks and radio shows use more prefixes than sports meets or airplanes do.
Recognizing the prefixes inter-, sub-, and non- helps you figure out long words.
Every word that starts with the letters non- is about a real fact or a flight.
Submarines and highways are the best examples of words borrowed from other lands.
qs.why: The reading explains each prefix with examples and concludes that spotting them gives readers a head start.
